title: Homeowners Section II and endorsements
summary: Learn Coverages E and F, the liability add-ons and watercraft rules, the outline's endorsements, and what Michigan's Special Provisions change.
objectives: Tell Coverage E from Coverage F, and know the Section II additional coverages
Apply the HO-3 watercraft rules and know when the Watercraft endorsement is needed
Match each selected endorsement to the gap it fills
Explain Michigan's innocent co-insured rule for a fire loss

scenes.title: Homeowners Section II and endorsements
scenes.subtitle: 2011 ISO HO-3 liability coverages, plus the endorsements on the exam outline

beats.text: This lesson covers homeowners liability, Coverages E and F, and the endorsements the exam outline lists, including Michigan's own.
beats.say: This lesson covers homeowners liability, Coverages E and F, and the endorsements the exam outline lists, including Michigan's own.

beats.text: Amounts come from the 2011 forms unless another edition is named.
beats.say: Amounts come from the twenty eleven forms unless another edition is named.

scenes.title: Coverage E vs Coverage F
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Coverages E–F; ISO HO Manual Table 301 (RIJRA)

columns.name: E: Personal Liability
points: Damages for bodily injury or property damage
Defense even if the suit is groundless
Defense ends when the limit is exhausted

columns.name: F: Medical Payments to Others
points: Medical expenses within 3 years of the accident
Not you or regular household residents

scenes.tell: E: 'Excuse me, you're being sued.' F: a Friend's Fall, not your household's bills (residence employees aside).

beats.text: Coverage E, Personal Liability, pays damages for bodily injury or property damage. It defends you even if the suit is groundless, false or fraudulent, until the limit is exhausted by a judgment or settlement.
beats.say: Coverage E, Personal Liability, pays damages for bodily injury or property damage. It defends you even if the suit is groundless, false or fraudulent, until the limit is exhausted by a judgment or settlement.

beats.text: Coverage F, Medical Payments to Others, pays medical expenses incurred within 3 years of the accident. It never covers you or regular residents of your household, except residence employees.
beats.say: Coverage F, Medical Payments to Others, pays medical expenses incurred within three years of the accident. It never covers you or regular residents of your household, except residence employees.

beats.text: Manual minimums: $100,000 for E, $1,000 per person for F. To remember them: E, excuse me, you're being sued. F, a friend's fall.
beats.say: Manual minimums: one hundred thousand dollars for E, one thousand dollars per person for F. To remember them: E, excuse me, you're being sued. F, a friend's fall.

scenes.title: Section II additional coverages
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Additional Coverages A–D

items.label: Claim expenses
items.detail: Defense costs, plus your lost earnings up to $250 a day

items.label: Damage to property of others
items.detail: $1,000 at replacement cost; not if intentional by an insured 13 or older

beats.text: Four additional coverages are paid on top of the limits. Claim expenses include your lost earnings, up to $250 a day. First aid to others is covered too.
beats.say: Four additional coverages are paid on top of the limits. Claim expenses include your lost earnings, up to two hundred fifty dollars a day. First aid to others is covered too.

beats.text: Damage to property of others pays up to $1,000 at replacement cost, but not for damage caused intentionally by an insured 13 or older, or for property an insured owns. Loss assessment adds $1,000.
beats.say: Damage to property of others pays up to one thousand dollars at replacement cost, but not for damage caused intentionally by an insured thirteen or older, or for property an insured owns. Loss assessment adds one thousand dollars.

scenes.q: Under the 2011 HO-3, which loss does the Damage to Property of Others additional coverage pay?
choices: Your 16-year-old intentionally breaks a neighbor's window
Your 9-year-old accidentally breaks a borrowed tablet
You accidentally damage your own snowblower
scenes.why: It pays up to $1,000 at replacement cost, but not for damage caused intentionally by an insured 13 or older, or for property owned by an insured.

beats.text: Quick check. Which of these does Damage to Property of Others pay? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check. Which of these does Damage to Property of Others pay? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The 9-year-old's accident. Intentional damage by an insured 13 or older isn't covered, and neither is property an insured owns.
reveal.say: The nine-year-old's accident. Intentional damage by an insured thirteen or older isn't covered, and neither is property an insured owns.

scenes.title: A boat on Houghton Lake
scenes.src: ISO HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Exclusions B.2; PF&M 2014 (HO 24 75)
scenes.story: Jake has a 2011 HO-3. He owns a fishing boat with a 40-horsepower outboard he bought three years ago and never declared or reported to his insurer. On Houghton Lake, he negligently injures a swimmer. Does Coverage E apply?

items.label: Owned outboards totaling 25 hp or less
Bigger owned outboard
items.detail: Only if acquired during the policy period, or declared at inception or reported within 45 days

items.label: Jake's 40 hp motor
items.detail: Owned earlier, never declared or reported: excluded

items.label: The fix
items.detail: Watercraft endorsement: liability for the described boat

scenes.answer: No. The watercraft exclusion applies. A Watercraft endorsement would add liability coverage for the boat.

beats.text: Jake owns a fishing boat with a 40-horsepower outboard. He bought it three years ago and never reported it. On Houghton Lake, he injures a swimmer. Does his HO-3 Coverage E apply?
beats.say: Jake owns a fishing boat with a forty horsepower outboard. He bought it three years ago and never reported it. On Houghton Lake, he injures a swimmer. Does his H O three Coverage E apply?

beats.text: Owned outboards totaling 25 horsepower or less are covered. A bigger one is covered only if acquired during the policy period, or declared at inception, or reported within 45 days after he acquired it.
beats.say: Owned outboards totaling twenty five horsepower or less are covered. A bigger one is covered only if acquired during the policy period, or declared at inception, or reported within forty five days after he acquired it.

beats.text: Jake's motor fails every test, so Coverage E does not apply. The Watercraft endorsement would add liability coverage for the boat, though not physical damage. An owned sailboat 26 feet or longer needs it too.
beats.say: Jake's motor fails every test, so Coverage E does not apply. The Watercraft endorsement would add liability coverage for the boat, though not physical damage. An owned sailboat twenty six feet or longer needs it too.

scenes.title: Property endorsements
items: Contents at RC; antiques stay at ACV
Shocks within 72 hours count as one

beats.text: Scheduled Personal Property covers listed classes, like jewelry, furs and fine arts, on open perils, worldwide, with no deductible.
beats.say: Scheduled Personal Property covers listed classes, like jewelry, furs and fine arts, on open perils, worldwide, with no deductible.

beats.text: Newly acquired jewelry in a class already scheduled is covered for 25% of that class's limit or $10,000, whichever is less, if reported within 30 days.
beats.say: Newly acquired jewelry in a class already scheduled is covered for twenty five percent of that class's limit or ten thousand dollars, whichever is less, if reported within thirty days.

beats.text: Personal Property Replacement Cost pays contents at replacement cost, but antiques, fine arts and collectors' items stay at actual cash value.
beats.say: Personal Property Replacement Cost pays contents at replacement cost, but antiques, fine arts and collectors' items stay at actual cash value.

beats.text: The 2000 Earthquake endorsement counts shocks within 72 hours as one earthquake. The 2002 Limited Fungi schedule shows $10,000 for property and $50,000 as a Coverage E aggregate.
beats.say: The two thousand Earthquake endorsement counts shocks within seventy two hours as one earthquake. The two thousand two Limited Fungi schedule shows ten thousand dollars for property and fifty thousand dollars as a Coverage E aggregate.

scenes.title: Liability and home business endorsements
items: Work liability of non-owners, like teachers
Business at home; still no BI to employees

beats.text: Coverage E pays for bodily injury and property damage, not personal injury. The Personal Injury endorsement adds libel, slander, false arrest, malicious prosecution, invasion of privacy, and wrongful eviction or entry.
beats.say: Coverage E pays for bodily injury and property damage, not personal injury. The Personal Injury endorsement adds libel, slander, false arrest, malicious prosecution, invasion of privacy, and wrongful eviction or entry.

beats.text: Business Pursuits covers an insured's business activities when the insured isn't the owner or a partner, like a teacher or a salesperson.
beats.say: Business Pursuits covers an insured's business activities when the insured isn't the owner or a partner, like a teacher or a salesperson.

beats.text: Paid day care for unrelated children is a business when it's an occupation, or paid more than $2,000 in the 12 months before the policy period. Then its liability is excluded. Home Day Care Coverage adds limited coverage back.
beats.say: Paid day care for unrelated children is a business when it's an occupation, or paid more than two thousand dollars in the twelve months before the policy period. Then its liability is excluded. Home Day Care Coverage adds limited coverage back.

beats.text: Permitted Incidental Occupancies covers a described business at home, like a piano studio, but not bodily injury to its employees. Home Business Insurance Coverage is a self-contained endorsement with property and liability coverage.
beats.say: Permitted Incidental Occupancies covers a described business at home, like a piano studio, but not bodily injury to its employees. Home Business Insurance Coverage is a self-contained endorsement with property and liability coverage.

scenes.q: A schoolteacher wants her homeowners policy to cover liability arising from her teaching job. Which endorsement fits?
scenes.why: Business Pursuits covers an insured's liability from business activities when the insured is not the owner or a partner, such as teachers, salespersons and clerical workers.

beats.text: Your turn. A schoolteacher wants liability coverage for her teaching job. Which endorsement fits? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Your turn. A schoolteacher wants liability coverage for her teaching job. Which endorsement fits? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Business Pursuits. She works for someone else and isn't an owner or partner. Home Business Insurance Coverage is for a business run at home.
reveal.say: Business Pursuits. She works for someone else and isn't an owner or partner. Home Business Insurance Coverage is for a business run at home.

scenes.title: Special Provisions – Michigan (HO 01 21)
scenes.src: MCL 500.2833(1)(q), (2); Wilson (E.D. Mich. 2019); FC&S summary of HO 01 21 05 11 (text not seen; 05 23 may differ)

items.label: Innocent co-insured, fire loss
items.detail: Covered up to his or her own interest; no domestic-abuse requirement

items.label: Who set the fire
items.detail: Not covered; the insurer may subrogate against that insured

items.label: Suit against the insurer
items.detail: 2 years, tolled from notice of loss until formal denial

beats.text: Now Michigan. The unendorsed form denies every insured for an intentional loss. But Michigan courts require coverage for an innocent co-insured's fire loss, and Michigan's endorsement covers that insured up to his or her own interest.
beats.say: Now Michigan. The unendorsed form denies every insured for an intentional loss. But Michigan courts require coverage for an innocent co-insured's fire loss, and Michigan's endorsement covers that insured up to his or her own interest.

beats.text: The insured who set the fire isn't covered. Suit is due within 2 years, tolled from notice of loss until formal denial. These points summarize the 2011 Michigan endorsement; newer editions may differ.
beats.say: The insured who set the fire isn't covered. Suit is due within two years, tolled from notice of loss until formal denial. These points summarize the twenty eleven Michigan endorsement; newer editions may differ.

scenes.q: Under a 2011 Michigan HO-3 with Special Provisions – Michigan, Dan intentionally sets fire to the home. His wife, Ana, took no part. Ana is:
choices: Not covered, because an insured caused the loss
Covered only if she is a victim of domestic abuse
Covered to the extent of her interest in the property
scenes.why: Michigan's endorsement covers an insured who is innocent of a fire loss to the extent of that insured's interest, with no domestic-abuse requirement.

beats.text: Last one. In Michigan, Dan intentionally burns the home. His wife, Ana, took no part. What coverage does Ana have? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Last one. In Michigan, Dan intentionally burns the home. His wife, Ana, took no part. What coverage does Ana have? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Covered to the extent of her interest. Michigan's endorsement requires no domestic-abuse showing. Dan isn't covered, and she doesn't collect his share.
reveal.say: Covered to the extent of her interest. Michigan's endorsement requires no domestic-abuse showing. Dan isn't covered, and she doesn't collect his share.

items: E: liability plus defense; F: others' medical bills within 3 years
Property of others: $1,000; not intentional by an insured 13 or older
Owned boats the form excludes need the Watercraft endorsement
Personal Injury for slander; Business Pursuits for employees
Michigan: innocent co-insured covered for fire, to extent of interest

beats.text: To recap. Coverage E pays damages and defense; Coverage F pays others' medical bills, not your household's, except residence employees. Damage to property of others pays up to $1,000.
beats.say: To recap. Coverage E pays damages and defense; Coverage F pays others' medical bills, not your household's, except residence employees. Damage to property of others pays up to one thousand dollars.

beats.text: Owned boats the form excludes, like Jake's, need the Watercraft endorsement. And in Michigan, an innocent co-insured is covered for a fire loss, up to her own interest.
beats.say: Owned boats the form excludes, like Jake's, need the Watercraft endorsement. And in Michigan, an innocent co-insured is covered for a fire loss, up to her own interest.
